rows.source: UKHSA avian-influenza public-health management
rows.verified: Avian influenza is an infectious disease of birds caused by influenza A viruses.

rows.source: UKHSA avian-influenza public-health management
rows.verified: Birds are hosts for most avian influenza viruses, with many subtypes found particularly in waterfowl and shore birds.

rows.source: UKHSA avian-influenza public-health management
rows.verified: Domestic poultry are especially vulnerable and avian influenza can spread rapidly within flocks.

rows.source: UKHSA avian-influenza public-health management
rows.verified: Human infections are rare, although some avian influenza viruses including H5N1 and H7N9 have caused human disease.

rows.source: UKHSA avian-influenza public-health management
rows.verified: UKHSA guidance distinguishes A(H5), other subtype exposures, sporadic human spillover cases and relevant overseas animal exposures.

rows.source: UKHSA avian-influenza public-health management
rows.verified: A(H5) exposure guidance covers animal case definitions, human exposure classification, PPE, antiviral use, testing and health-protection actions.

rows.source: UKHSA avian-influenza public-health management
rows.verified: Members of the public should avoid touching injured, sick or dead wild birds where possible and follow risk-reduction guidance if contact cannot be avoided.

rows.source: UKHSA avian-influenza public-health management
rows.verified: Bird-keeper biosecurity includes preventing wild-bird contact, separating groups, cleaning and disinfecting housing, controlling pests and managing clothing and footwear.

rows.source: UKHSA avian-influenza public-health management
rows.verified: Avian-influenza risk depends on viral subtype, animal species, exposure intensity, PPE, symptoms, antiviral timing, host factors and local epidemiology.

rows.source: UKHSA avian-influenza public-health management
rows.verified: UKHSA avian-influenza evidence is subtype-, animal-, exposure-, person-, incident- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.

rows.source: UKHSA typhoid and paratyphoid public-health management
rows.verified: Typhoid and paratyphoid are enteric-fever diseases caused by Salmonella Typhi or Salmonella Paratyphi A, B and C.

rows.source: UKHSA typhoid and paratyphoid public-health management
rows.verified: Classic typhoid fever is a serious disease and can be life-threatening unless treated promptly with antibiotics.

rows.source: UKHSA typhoid and paratyphoid public-health management
rows.verified: Paratyphoid is typically milder and shorter in duration than typhoid.

rows.source: UKHSA typhoid and paratyphoid public-health management
rows.verified: UK cases are almost exclusively acquired abroad through ingestion of heavily contaminated food or water.

rows.source: UKHSA typhoid and paratyphoid public-health management
rows.verified: Enteric fever is prevalent in regions where sanitation is poor.

rows.source: UKHSA typhoid and paratyphoid public-health management
rows.verified: Public-health guidance supports identifying the source of infection and reducing secondary transmission.

rows.source: UKHSA typhoid and paratyphoid public-health management
rows.verified: The response package includes operational guidelines, local-response algorithms, enhanced questionnaires and microbiological-clearance documentation.

rows.source: UKHSA typhoid and paratyphoid public-health management
rows.verified: The operational guidance includes updated wording for clearance for public-health purposes.

rows.source: UKHSA typhoid and paratyphoid public-health management
rows.verified: Enteric-fever risk depends on destination, sanitation, food and water exposure, organism, symptoms, antimicrobial resistance, occupation and clearance status.

rows.source: UKHSA typhoid and paratyphoid public-health management
rows.verified: UKHSA enteric-fever evidence is traveller-, exposure-, organism-, patient-, public-health-action- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
